zebralogic.title: DirectAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that X is directly left/right of Y, enforce that the house numbers differ by exactly one and respect the direction.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Clues containing phrases like "directly left of", "directly right of", or "immediately to the left/right of".
zebralogic.example: Treating "directly left of" as merely "somewhere to the left of", allowing any distance between X and Y.

zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says X is somewhere to the left/right of Y, enforce a strict ordering X < Y (or X > Y) without assuming adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Clues with phrases like "somewhere to the left of", "to the right of", "is to the left of", etc.
zebralogic.example: Assuming X must be immediately adjacent to Y when the clue only says "somewhere to the left of", which over‑constrains the solution.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., "the person who smokes X is Y"), link those values so they refer to the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Clues that directly associate two attributes, such as "X is Y", "the person who ... is ...", or "the ... who ... is ...".
zebralogic.example: Failing to link "the person who smokes Yellow Monster" with "the mother whose child is Meredith", treating them as separate entities.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number, assign that attribute to that house and propagate the constraint to all other attributes.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Clues that specify a house number, e.g., "the root beer lover is in the first house" or "the tea drinker lives in house 5".
zebralogic.example: Ignoring a fixed house assignment and leaving the attribute free, which yields multiple possible solutions.

zebralogic.title: ValidateJSONStructureAndSyntax
zebralogic.principle: Before final output, ensure the JSON object is syntactically valid: proper brackets, commas, double quotes, and correct nesting.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: At the very end of the response, just before submitting the answer.
zebralogic.example: Producing malformed JSON with missing commas or mismatched brackets, causing the verifier to reject the answer.

zebralogic.title: CompactFinalAnswer
zebralogic.principle: Place the solution JSON as the very last part of the response, with any reasoning before it, so the verifier extracts the answer correctly.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When formatting the final answer for the puzzle.
zebralogic.example: Appending explanatory text after the JSON, causing the verifier to miss the solution block.

zebralogic.title: ExactHouseDistance
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says there are N houses between X and Y, enforce that the absolute difference in house numbers is N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Clues with phrasing like "there is one house between", "two houses between", etc.
zebralogic.example: Using a difference of N instead of N + 1, placing X and Y only one house apart when the clue required one house in between.

zebralogic.title: NegativeHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that a particular attribute value is not in a specific house, ensure that assignment is prohibited.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Clues containing "not in house", "cannot be", "is not", etc.
zebralogic.example: Placing the child Fred in house 4 despite a clue explicitly forbidding it.

zebralogic.title: UndirectedAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says X and Y are next to each other without specifying direction, enforce that their house numbers differ by exactly one, regardless of order.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Clues with "next to each other", "are adjacent", "are side by side", etc.
zebralogic.example: Treating undirected adjacency as a directed adjacency, thereby fixing an incorrect order between X and Y.

zebralogic.title: CanonicalCaseMatching
zebralogic.principle: When outputting attribute values, match the exact case (e.g., lower‑casing) as given in the problem statement.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During final answer construction, for every attribute value.
zebralogic.example: Outputting "May" instead of the required "may", causing a mismatch with the expected answer.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting 'N houses between' as 'N houses apart' (using a difference of N instead of N+1).
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses the phrase "between" with a simple distance, forgetting that "N houses between" implies an extra house separating the two entities.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue mentions "N houses between X and Y", enforce |pos(X) - pos(Y)| = N + 1.

zebralogic.description: Placing the solution JSON before the end of the response or adding excessive text after it, causing truncation or the verifier to miss the answer.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model does not respect the required placement of the final answer and may continue generating commentary after the JSON block.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Ensure the JSON solution is the very last part of the response, with no extra characters or text following it.

zebralogic.description: Exceeding token limit causing the final answer to be truncated.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model generates overly long reasoning or repeats, surpassing the allowed token budget, which cuts off the JSON output.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep reasoning concise and verify that the final answer fits comfortably within the token limit before submitting.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring negative house constraints (placing an attribute in a house that a clue explicitly forbids).
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model overlooks or forgets clues that prohibit a specific attribute from occupying a particular house.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Track all "not in house" constraints during solving and enforce them when assigning values.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model does not preserve the exact capitalization of attribute strings as presented in the problem.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute values verbatim from the problem statement, preserving their case, when constructing the final JSON.
